reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch deny that Abraham's Dan is the Laish later renamed Dan, identifying it instead as a separate Gileadite town called Dan-Jaan.

discrepancy.note: Paine argues the city bore no such name in Abraham's day, making the Genesis reference to Dan proof of a later author.

quotes.text: there was no such place as Dan till many years after the death of Moses; and consequently, that Moses could not be the writer of the book of Genesis, where this account of pursuing them unto Dan is given.
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II (1795), ch. I, on Genesis 14:14 and Judges 18:29.

sides.snippet: he led forth his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.
sides.verseText: When Abram heard that his relative was taken captive, he led forth his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.

sides.snippet: however the name of the city was Laish at the first.
sides.verseText: They called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel: however the name of the city was Laish at the first.
